section: Perspectives in Education · Ch19 — NEP 2020 (Complete Coverage)
subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: NEP 2020 proposes an 'Academic Bank of Credits' (ABC) mainly to allow students to:

options.option_text: Store credits earned from different institutions/programmes digitally and transfer them, enabling multiple entry/exit in degree programmes
Deposit money for tuition fees only
Receive scholarships automatically with no application

explanation: The Academic Bank of Credits digitally stores academic credits earned across institutions, enabling flexible multiple entry/exit points in higher education degree programmes — a credit-transfer mechanism, not a financial account.

stem: PARAKH, a national assessment body proposed under NEP 2020, is primarily tasked with:

options.option_text: Setting norms, standards and guidelines for student assessment across school boards

explanation: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) is envisioned as a national assessment centre setting standards to bring parity across varied school-board assessment systems.

subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: NEP 2020 envisions that, by 2030, the minimum degree qualification for teaching will be a:

options.option_text: 1-year B.Ed. only, with no other option
No formal degree requirement at all

explanation: NEP 2020 proposes a 4-year integrated B.Ed. as the standard minimum teacher qualification by 2030, phasing out other, shorter teacher-education routes over time.

subject: Perspectives in Education
stem: The concept of 'School Complexes' proposed under NEP 2020 involves:

options.option_text: Clustering a group of nearby schools (of different levels) to share resources, teachers and facilities
Building one enormous single school for an entire district
Closing all small schools with no alternative
Separating schools completely with no resource sharing

explanation: School Complexes group a secondary school with nearby primary/upper-primary schools to enable shared resources (labs, libraries, specialist teachers) — especially useful for small, resource-constrained rural schools, rather than simply merging or closing them.
